message: All 26 contract clauses (REQ-SC-1..26) are INFERRED by the planner rather than AUTHORED by rust-contract. The plan §2 explicitly admits this gap: 'The bead cl-zup has no upstream rust-contract artifact under clarity-web/src/domain/contract.md'. All 33 planned obligations carry requires_contract: true. Every Verus spec the proof-writer will author is grounded in clauses the planner guessed at by reading source. Per go-skill workflow, rust-contract MUST precede proof-planner; the planner here ran in reverse. The plan §9 item 1 names this BLOCKING. This is a workspace-wide condition affecting all 8 module plans per formal-verification-report.md §3, but scenario.rs is particularly exposed because the central open questions (Q1 'addressed' semantics, Q2 whitespace semantics in bullets) drive 7 of the 26 clauses (REQ-SC-11, -12, -14, -15, -16, -21, -22).
required_fix: 1. rust-contract produces clarity-web/src/domain/contract.md (or per-module analogue) authoring REQ-SC-1..26 with explicit decisions on the 5 open questions in plan §3. 2. The 33 obligation rows in scenario-obligations.planned.jsonl have clause_origin flipped from INFERRED to AUTHORED and requires_contract: false. 3. Re-submit to proof-plan-reviewer.
blocker_reason: No rust-contract artifact exists. All 33 obligations reference inferred clauses. Proof-writer cannot author Verus specs or proptest properties against unratified contract clauses without producing work that may be invalidated by a single contract-ratification decision. The plan §3 explicitly enumerates 5 open questions whose resolution changes the proof shape for 7 of the 26 clauses.

message: Plan §3 lists 5 'Open questions for rust-contract' and §9 item 2 labels them 'NON-BLOCKING but recommended'. This is wrong. Q1 (addressed semantics) and Q2 (whitespace semantics in bullets) are behavior-affecting: they drive 7 clauses total (REQ-SC-11, -12, -14, -15, -16, -21, -22) and change the proof shape (the 'addressed' definition in particular is the central predicate of L5, L6, L13, L14, L15, L16). A Verus spec written for 'Some(s) && !s.trim().is_empty()' is structurally different from one written for 'Some(_)'. Proptest strategies are also affected. The other three questions (Q3-Q5) are non-blocking in the sense that they produce additive or shape-preserving changes.
required_fix: Reclassify Q1 and Q2 as BLOCKING in plan §3 and §9. The two cannot be deferred; they must be resolved by rust-contract before proof-writer drafts any spec touching REQ-SC-11..16 or REQ-SC-21..22. Q3-Q5 may remain non-blocking with their proposed additive solutions.
blocker_reason: Q1 'addressed' semantics determines the truth value of REQ-SC-12 is_addressed and propagates through REQ-SC-13 is_complete, REQ-SC-14 address single-call, REQ-SC-15 right-most-wins, REQ-SC-16 idempotent. Changing this from 'Some(s) && !s.trim().is_empty()' to 'Some(_)' rewrites 5 of the 25 Verus specs and 3 of the 8 proptest properties. Q2 whitespace semantics similarly rewrites REQ-SC-21/22. These are not 'recommended'; they are gating.

message: Plan §6 enumerates 10 trust entries (String::trim, u8::clamp, serde_json round-trip, Vec::push, Display::fmt for &str, HoleType closed enum, struct-literal closed shapes, address #[must_use], no Hash/Ord derives on the two structs). Per go-skill proof-schemas.md, every trust boundary (assume, axiom, admit, external_body, trusted, ignore, stub, disabled check, model bound, model reduction) needs ONE trusted-base-ledger/v1 row. The plan produces a prose list, not the JSONL ledger. Proof-writer cannot honour the ledger without these rows.
required_fix: Proof-writer (or planner) produces trusted-base-ledger/v1 JSONL with one row per trust entry enumerated in §6. Each row must include schema_version, id, obligation_id (the consuming obligation), artifact, location, marker, trusted_kind, reason, scope, impact, behavior_affecting, compensating_evidence (linking to the corresponding proptest row where applicable), owner, expiry, reviewer_disposition, status. The trusted_kind for the Display::fmt external_body is 'external_body' per Verus semantics. The trusted_kind for String::trim/u8::clamp/serde_json is 'extern_spec'. The struct-literal closed-shape entries are 'type-system-fact' (not actually a runtime trust boundary; document them as 'model_completeness' or similar to make the distinction visible).
blocker_reason: Without the ledger, proof-writer cannot enumerate the trust boundaries in the verifier output. formal-verifier cannot validate that every extern_spec and external_body has a ledger row. The plan §6 prose is well-written but is not the machine-readable artifact the workflow requires.

message: Plan §8 'Bridge input for proof-to-implementation' is a Markdown table mapping Verus claims to Rust source refs and existing tests. This is a useful pre-stage but does not satisfy the rust-refinement-obligation/v1 schema per proof-schemas.md. The bridge agent will need to materialize one rust-refinement-obligation/v1 row per behavior-affecting Verus obligation (25 rows for PO-SC-V-01..25). The plan §8 contains the data needed but does not produce the rows. This is a planning-stage miss that pushes work downstream to proof-to-implementation, which then runs without prior reviewer sign-off.
required_fix: Either (a) planner pre-stages rust-refinement-obligation/v1 rows now (extending the JSONL), or (b) proof-writer produces them after ratification, with proof-plan-reviewer reviewing the bridge outputs before evidence-packaging. Option (a) is preferred because it gives proof-to-implementation a fully-spec'd input. If (a), add a new file proofs/scenario-refinement-obligations.planned.jsonl with one row per PO-SC-V-01..25 (and possibly PO-SC-P-01..08 if proptest is considered a refinement).
blocker_reason: Per the workflow, every behavior-affecting Verus obligation needs a matching rust-refinement-obligation with concrete source_refs, behavior_test_refs, refinement_harness_refs, and an evidence_command. Plan §8 contains the first three columns but not the evidence_command or the JSONL envelope. Without these, proof-to-implementation will improvise without prior sign-off.

message: Plan §6 trusted-base row 8 reads: 'address(self, ht, e) is #[must_use] (line 196 doc-comment) — but the function is total and side-effect-free on the consumed self' and the 'Why trusted' column states 'no #[must_use] attribute is actually present at line 196 (only the doc comment)'. The source has #[must_use]] at line 198 (with line 197 being the doc comment '/// Empty strings are normalized to None.'). The plan is internally contradictory: 'is #[must_use]]' in the trust description and 'no #[must_use]] attribute is actually present' in the mitigation. The substance is correct (the attribute IS present and the function IS total) but the citation is off by 2 lines and the self-contradiction is confusing.
required_fix: Correct the line number to 198 (or whatever the post-ratification line number is). Remove the contradictory 'is #[must_use]] / no #[must_use]] attribute' phrasing; replace with a single sentence noting the attribute is present and the function is observably total on the consumed self.
blocker_reason: Internal contradiction in the trusted-base plan is a documentation defect that propagates to proof-writer and ledger. Must be fixed before approval.

message: Plan §5 row PO-SC-V-18 (unaddressed_holes idempotence) asserts 'idempotence via pure observer' as a Verus property. This is trivially true for any function with signature `&self -> Vec<HoleType>`; the type system already guarantees that calling a pure observer twice without mutation produces equal results. The Verus spec adds nothing beyond what the Rust borrow checker already proves. The same property is redundantly covered by proptest PO-SC-P-03. Either downgrade PO-SC-V-18 to a one-line external_body assertion (no real proof) or remove the idempotence sub-claim and rely on the existing filter/collect spec.
required_fix: Either (a) drop the idempotence sub-claim from PO-SC-V-18's contract clause and expected_evidence, leaving only the filter/collect spec and the 0..=3 range bound, or (b) justify the Verus spec with a non-trivial postcondition (e.g. 'result.len() == (3 - addressed_count())', which is non-obvious and worth proving).
rationale: Trivially-true postconditions are not a verifier failure; they are a proof-cost efficiency issue. The debt is bounded by PO-SC-V-18 alone. Acceptable to keep as-is if proof-writer adds no extra ceremony beyond a one-line ensures.

message: Plan §5 row PO-SC-V-23 bundles three distinct functions into a single Verus obligation: 'is_trigger_empty, is_value_moment_empty, is_feeling_empty'. The expected_evidence says '(one obligation covering all 3)'. Per the verification-ledger/v1 schema, each obligation closure row should map to one function. Bundling three functions into one obligation makes per-function ledger closure impossible and obscures which function failed if Verus rejects. The three functions are structurally identical but are separate public API surface.
required_fix: Split PO-SC-V-23 into three rows: PO-SC-V-23a (is_trigger_empty), PO-SC-V-23b (is_value_moment_empty), PO-SC-V-23c (is_feeling_empty). Each row targets one function and carries one closure in the ledger.
blocker_reason: Bundling breaks the per-function ledger closure model. Verifier cannot report which of the three functions failed if Verus rejects the spec. Must split before approval.

message: The obligations JSONL uses schema_version='proof-obligations/v1' (plural). The canonical schema per go-skill/references/proof-schemas.md is 'proof-obligation/v1' (singular). This is a schema version drift that will cause validator rejection downstream.
required_fix: Bulk-update all 40 rows in scenario-obligations.planned.jsonl to use schema_version='proof-obligation/v1' (singular).
blocker_reason: Schema drift is a hard validator rejection. Must fix before approval.

message: Plan §9 item 4 acknowledges that the new `#[cfg(test)] mod tests_proptest` submodule must stay clippy-clean and may need `#[allow(...)]` mirroring the existing test module (lines 326-340). The verification-targets.md §10 / formal-verification-report.md §3 establishes that clarity-web/Cargo.toml has no [lints] opt-in, but scenario.rs itself has module-level `#![warn(clippy::unwrap_used)]`, `#![warn(clippy::expect_used)]`, `#![warn(clippy::panic)]`, `#![warn(clippy::pedantic)]`, `#![warn(clippy::nursery)]` (lines 1-5). These override the parent domain/mod.rs deny rules. proptest bodies using `vec![]`, `String::new()`, or other pedantic-friction constructs will trip clippy::pedantic and clippy::nursery warnings even if they don't trip unwrap/expect/panic. The plan correctly identifies the mitigation but does not enumerate which specific clippy lints the new proptest submodule must allow.
required_fix: In plan §9 item 4, enumerate the specific lints to allow in the proptest submodule (e.g. clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::needless_pass_by_value, clippy::unnecessary_debug_formatting, plus any pedantic-friction lints expected to trip on proptest idiom like clippy::redundant_field_names). Reference the existing test module's allow list at lines 326-340 as the template.
blocker_reason: Plan is honest about the exposure but does not enumerate the specific lint set. proof-writer will improvise; clippy gate may catch the additions and block CI. Must enumerate before approval.

Verified: (1) Axis A bullets decompose via !is_trigger_empty && !is_value_moment_empty && !is_feeling_empty (source lines 300-304, 308-322); (2) Axis B hole-punching decomposes via 3 is_addressed checks (source lines 175-191, 159-172); (3) terminal state is Complete == BulletsComplete × HolesComplete (source line 294-296); (4) no rejected/failed state — predicates return false, value stays partial. Laws L1-L9 verified: L1 right-most-wins (line 199-203, single field write), L2 idempotent (L1 + e1==e2), L3 addressed_count monotonic (line 229-234, pure observer + address never decrements), L4 unaddressed_holes idempotent (line 219-225, pure), L5 is_complete == bullets ∧ hole-punching complete (line 294-296), L6 is_complete == addressed_count == 3 ∧ bullets_complete (line 159-172 vs 229-234), L7 is_bullets_complete == !is_trigger_empty ∧ ... (line 300-304 vs 308-322), L8 HoleType::all canonical (line 37-43), L9 with_severity clamp [1,5] (line 107).
rationale: State machine analysis and L1-L9 laws verified accurate to source. Strongest aspect of the plan.

Lines 535 and 628 unwraps are in the #[cfg(test)] mod tests block. The plan's claim 'scenario.rs production function bodies contribute zero to the cl-2q6 baseline' is VERIFIED.

Recommend that proof-planner explicitly cite the per-module warn overrides in scenario.rs lines 1-5 as the mechanism that keeps scenario.rs clean (other domain modules like straw_man.rs have similar overrides but the test-only module opens the same lints).

message: Plan §4 lane decisions are sound. TLA+ rejection (§4 row T) is correctly argued: the state machine is predicate-driven over immutable values; no internal mutable state, no event log, no scheduler, no retries, no leases, no batch ordering. A TLA+ spec would describe client-side sequencing, not module behaviour, and would be vacuous for the module-internal guarantees. Flux downgrade (§4 row F) is correctly argued: Option<String> and unconstrained String cannot directly carry refinement indices without type restructure. 25 Verus + 8 proptest is appropriate density for a ~325 LOC production state machine (1 obligation per ~10 LOC; under the per-function ratio for algebraic-state-machine modules).
rationale: Lane discipline is the strongest non-state-machine aspect of the plan. TLA+ rejection is principled, not convenience.
